- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly, especially in early/medium horizon.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or mixed, model often underestimates; increase forecast, particularly if recent price action shows upward momentum.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +5+ points in 1-2 days); apply downward correction in next 3-5 days, especially if sentiment turns neutral or negative.
- If sentiment shifts from negative to positive mid-horizon, model often fails to adjust; re-forecast with upward bias only if sentiment confirms sustained bullishness.
- Mean reversion bias: if model forecasts >+10% above recent 10-day average, reduce forecast by 5-10% unless sentiment strongly supports continuation.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts often overreact to short-term sentiment; dampen early forecast peaks if sentiment is volatile or mixed.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “+0.33” or “+0.67” in 3+ consecutive days, model tends to lag; adjust forecast upward by 1-3% to match sentiment momentum.
